sources.name: California DMV - Motorcycles, Mopeds, and Scooters (registration page)
sources.contains: DMV plain-language definitions of motorcycle (CVC 400), motor-driven cycle (CVC 405), moped/motorized bicycle (CVC 406), motorized scooter (CVC 407.5); registration, license class, insurance, age, helmet requirements per class
headline_datapoints: Moped (CVC 406): 'A moped has 2-3 wheels and an electric motor with an automatic transmission that produces less than 4 gross brake horsepower.' Requires M1 or M2 license; registration required with special plate/ID card; '$23 one-time registration fee'; DMV states insurance is not required to register a moped; min age 16; helmet required.
Motor-driven cycle (CVC 405): DMV paraphrase 'engine size smaller than 149 cc'; registration required, M1 license required, insurance required.

Motorcycle (CVC 400): DMV paraphrase 'engine size larger than 150 cc'; registration + insurance required. NOTE: the WebFetch summary table rendered the motorcycle license row as 'Class C (or M1 for 3-wheel)', which is almost certainly inverted (Class C covers 3-wheel/sidecar; 2-wheel motorcycle needs M1) - verify directly on the page.

sources.name: SB 1271 (2024) - Electric bicycles, powered mobility devices, and storage batteries (bill text, leginfo)
sources.contains: Amended CVC 312.5 e-bike definition (fully operable pedals, motor 750 W or less, throttle only on Class 2 capped at 20 mph); battery/e-bike/charging-system accredited-lab certification requirement for sale or lease; State Fire Marshal rulemaking mandate
sources.year: 2024 (definition changes effective 2025-01-01; battery certification effective 2026-01-01 per secondary sources)
headline_datapoints: Snippet: 'Commencing January 1, 2026, the State Fire Marshal must adopt regulations promoting fire and electrical safety of electric bicycles and powered mobility devices, and prohibits distributing, selling, or leasing electric bicycles or powered mobility devices unless the storage battery has been tested by an accredited testing laboratory for compliance with a specified standard.'
Secondary summary: certification to UL 2849 or EN 15194 (or an OSFM-adopted standard); product must carry permanent mark showing testing lab and standard met.
Secondary summary: 'Anything over 750W (or capable of over 20 mph on motor power alone) doesn't meet California's e-bike definition and legally can't be sold or labeled as one.'

sources.name: AB 545 (2025) - e-bike classification clarification (LegiScan chaptered text; Assembly Transportation analysis)
sources.contains: 2025 follow-on to SB 1271 clarifying e-bike classification; Assembly Transportation committee analysis at https://atrn.assembly.ca.gov/system/files/2025-04/ab-545-davies.pdf
headline_datapoints: Snippet: 'Approved by Governor July 14, 2025. This bill follows a similar bill from 2024 that clarified California's e-bike classification system and further defines e-bikes as having fully operable pedals and a motor of 750 watts or less.'

sources.name: SB 455 (2025-2026, Blakespear) - Electric bicycles / 'low-power moped' labeling (leginfo bill page)

headline_datapoints: Snippet: 'This bill revises the definitions of described devices and refers to motorized bicycles as mopeds or low-power mopeds, and commencing July 1, 2026, requires manufacturers and distributors of low-power mopeds to apply an etching, an engraving, or a label that is permanently affixed to each low-power moped that contains a statement that the device is a low-power moped and not an electric bicycle.'

must_ask_hmp: For each product (HMP FLASH, Lightning MK.II, SWFT MAXX, each e-bike model): rated motor watts / gross brake hp, top speed on motor alone, throttle presence, pedal presence, and how it is currently classified and registered with the DMV in SF (e-bike / CVC 406 moped plate / CVC 405 motor-driven cycle / CVC 400 motorcycle), plus whether each has a 17-digit VIN, MCO, DOT/FMVSS and CARB documentation.

Which certification (UL 2849 / UL 2271 / EN 15194 / UL 2272) each product and each swap battery/charger currently holds, and the accredited lab and marking - required for any CA sale or lease from 2026-01-01 under SB 1271.

How SF couriers on HMP vehicles currently sign up on Uber Eats and DoorDash (bike vs scooter vs motorcycle mode), whether Uber has accepted FLASH/Lightning as '<50cc scooters', and observed differences in order radius/pay by mode.

Current SF insurance program: carrier/broker, coverage form (GL, physical damage, renter liability, hired/non-owned), premium per vehicle by tier, and whether renters carry their own 30/60/15 policies for registered vehicles.
Current SF battery storage/charging setup (kWh on site, charger count, room construction, SFFD permits held) to compare against 2025 CFC / LAFD requirements at 768 Ceres Ave.
Share of current riders holding an M1 or M2 license; whether HMP assists with licensing (affects feasibility of tiers B-D).
surprises: Uber Eats' Los Angeles sign-up page lists only car, scooter ('motorized scooter under 50cc', age 21, driver's license), bicycle and on-foot - no motorcycle mode. Secondary sources state 'motorcycles typically won't qualify'. This undercuts the prior belief that LA favors 40-70 mph vehicles, at least for Uber Eats couriers, unless HMP has evidence Uber accepts electric mopeds under the 50cc rule.

Tier B (28-35 mph) is not an e-bike in California at all: after SB 1271 (2024) / AB 545 (2025), an e-bike must have operable pedals, a motor of 750 W or less, throttle only on Class 2 capped at 20 mph; anything faster on motor power is a moped/motor-driven cycle needing M1/M2 license, DMV plate and helmet, and from 2026-01-01 police can impound non-compliant high-power two-wheelers (AB 875, per secondary summary).

Tiers C and D (40-70+ mph) cannot be CVC 406 mopeds (moped definition capped at 30 mph per prior knowledge - verify); they are motor-driven cycles or motorcycles requiring an M1 license, annual registration, and mandatory liability insurance whose minimums doubled to 30/60/15 on 2025-01-01 (SB 1107) - a per-rider licensing and insurance barrier not present for SF's 20 mph e-bike fleet.

Even the moped tier (CVC 406) requires an M1 or M2 license and DMV registration ($23 one-time fee); DoorDash's bike mode requires no license, so any move above 20/28 mph shrinks the eligible courier pool to licensed riders.

SB 1271's battery certification requirement applies to leasing, not just selling, from 2026-01-01 - HMP's LA rental fleet and swap batteries must carry accredited-lab marks (UL 2849/EN 15194 or OSFM-accepted standard); California has effectively adopted the NYC Local Law 39 approach statewide.

The 2025 California Fire Code took effect 2026-01-01 with a new Section 320 on battery storage replacing 2022 Section 322 - the fire-code baseline for 768 Ceres Ave is the 2025 CFC (IFC 2024 basis), not the 2022 code most consultant guidance still cites.

SB 455 (if enacted as amended) would require a permanent 'low-power moped, not an electric bicycle' label from manufacturers/distributors commencing 2026-07-01 - directly affects how HMP labels FLASH-class products sold in CA.
DoorDash does offer a Motorcycle dash type (market-dependent), so DoorDash - not Uber Eats - may be the only major platform where tiers C-D are usable; availability in LA unconfirmed.
